subtopics.title: Constitution and Role of the Commission
subtopics.summary: The 16th Finance Commission was set up in 2023 under Article 280 to recommend how tax revenue is distributed between the Centre and the States. It has one Chairperson, Dr. Arvind Panagariya, and four other members, appointed by the President for a generally five-year tenure. Its report and an Action Taken Memorandum are laid before Parliament under Article 281, and the Government has accepted its key recommendations for 2026-31.
facts: Set up in 2023 under Article 280 of the Constitution
Constitutional body that recommends distribution of tax revenues between Centre and States
Chairperson: Dr. Arvind Panagariya, former Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog
Other members: Ajay Narayan Jha, Annie George Mathew, Niranjan Rajadhyaksha, Soumya Kanti Ghosh
Composition: 1 Chairperson and 4 other members
Constituted by the President of India, every five years or earlier if required
Members appointed for a specified tenure, generally 5 years
Report and Action Taken Memorandum laid before Parliament under Article 281
Report tabled in Lok Sabha by the Union Finance Minister
Central Government is not bound by Finance Commission suggestions

subtopics.title: Grants-in-Aid, Cess and Surcharge
subtopics.summary: Statutory grants under Article 275 go only to States in need of financial assistance and are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India every year. Discretionary grants under Article 282 can be made for any public purpose, and the Centre has no obligation to give them. Cesses and surcharges are levied by the Centre and are not shared with States, while SASCI provides long-term interest-free loans for capital projects.
facts: Statutory grants under Article 275: Parliament makes grants to States in need of financial assistance
Statutory grants are not given to every State
Statutory grants are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India every year
Discretionary grants under Article 282 can be made for any public purpose
Discretionary grants can be made even outside legislative competence
Centre has no obligation to give discretionary grants
Cess: a 'tax on tax' levied for specific purposes such as education and health
Cess is mandatory for all taxpayers and is not shared with States
Surcharge: additional tax on high-income earners, not shared with States
SASCI launched in 2020-21 gives 50-year interest-free loans to States for capital projects

subtopics.title: Impact, Concerns and Past Commissions
subtopics.summary: The retained 41 per cent share is said to give States revenue predictability, and the revised formula is said to safeguard fiscally weaker States. Critics point to the 41 per cent share falling short of the 50 per cent demanded, the reduced weight for demographic performance, and the discontinuation of revenue-deficit grants. Finance Commissions have been appointed since 1951, and the early chairpersons include K.C. Neogy.
facts: Retaining 41% vertical devolution gives States revenue predictability
Revised horizontal formula is said to safeguard fiscally weaker States
Concern: States' share stays at 41% despite demands for 50%
Concern: lower weight to income distance and new GDP criterion may favour richer, populous States
Concern: reduced demographic weight raises 'Ageing Before Prosperity' fears, especially in Southern States
Concern: discontinuing revenue-deficit grants could hurt Hill and Special-category States
Concern: cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool reduce untied fiscal space for States
First Finance Commission (1951) chaired by K.C. Neogy
Eighth Finance Commission (1982) chaired by Y.B. Chavan
Fifteenth Finance Commission (2017) chaired by N.K. Singh
